question: Can I use the counseling service, and how do I register?
required_facts: Yes: OIA counseling is for international students (individual and group counseling, psychological testing), in Korean, Chinese and English
Seoul: visit the OIA or e-mail, fill in the application form, then an interview/test (02-2220-2450, International Building 218, Mon-Fri 9-17)
ERICA: free 3-phase counseling for all international students, booked through HY-in > Application > Personal Counseling/Psychological Testing
reference_answer: Yes, international students, including visiting students, can use the counseling service. At Seoul, visit the OIA or send an e-mail, fill in the application form and take an interview or test before counseling (02-2220-2450, International Building room 218, Mon-Fri 9:00-17:00; Korean, Chinese or English). At ERICA, the 3-phase counseling is free for all international students and is booked on HY-in under Application > Personal Counseling/Psychological Testing.
notes: Campus unstated and the booking procedure differs; two branches (11.6) -> conditional_answer, clarify acceptable.

question: Can I live in the dorm and how do I apply?
required_facts: ERICA: priority goes to new students entering Korea for the first time; apply on HY-in > Apply > Dormitory Application (January-February / July-August)
Seoul: new undergraduates apply on the dormitory application page (log in with application number); rooms first-come, first-served, only for the first semester
Students not assigned a room must find their own housing (Seoul)
reference_answer: Yes, new international students can apply for a dorm. At ERICA, new students entering Korea for the first time get priority; you apply on HY-in (Apply > Dormitory Application, choose building and room type) in the January-February or July-August window. At Seoul, rooms for new undergraduates are first-come, first-served and only for the first semester; you apply on the dormitory application page with your application number, and students without a room must find their own housing.
notes: Campus unstated (persona ERICA); procedures differ -> 2 branches. ERICA how-to is from the 2025 Spring notice (stable procedure); Seoul from the 2026 Fall acceptance guideline.

question: How do I go on leave and then return?
required_facts: Leave: apply online in HY-in > Application > Leave of Absence and upload a copy of passport and residence card; no in-person applications
After taking leave you must leave Korea within 30 days
Return: apply online in HY-in during the return period with passport copy, the ERICA OIA return form and a bank balance certificate (original must reach the ERICA OIA)
Undergraduates can take at most 1 year at a time; not returning after the leave expires leads to expulsion
reference_answer: To go on leave, apply online on HY-in (Application > Leave of Absence) and upload your passport and residence card; OIA does not accept in-person applications, and you must leave Korea within 30 days. As an undergraduate you can take up to 1 year at a time. To return, apply on HY-in during the return-to-school period with a passport copy, the ERICA OIA return form and a bank balance certificate whose original must reach the ERICA OIA; if you do not return when your leave expires, you are expelled.
notes: Campus unstated; Seoul return is also online via HY-in with passport + bank certificate, so treated as same procedure (no split). Earlier ERICA guides in outdated.
